expected_findings.validation_notes: TLS-001 fires on the [legacy] domain config even though no listener references it. v1.0 engine is not configuration-aware about which domains are bound; rule treats all domain configs equally.
Fires on the unreachable route[unused_legacy_relay] because v1.0 engine is not path-sensitive. Per 14_DETECTION_ENGINE.md § 'Open issues', unreachable code is treated as reachable.

RELAY-001 should fire on the t_relay() in route[unused_legacy_relay] (no preceding guard in that route block). The semantic judge sees no permissions/allow_routing in the dead route's scope and confirms. The t_relay in request_route's main path is properly guarded by is_myself + has_totag and should not fire.
Fires on route[debug_dump] which is never invoked. v1.0 contract: dead code still flagged.

validation_notes: v1.0 contract: this fixture exercises the deliberately-conservative 'no path sensitivity' choice in 14_DETECTION_ENGINE.md § 'Open issues'. Dead routes that would be vulnerable IF reached are flagged as findings.

If a future engine version adds path-sensitivity, this fixture's expected output will change — F2, F3, F4 should be moved to a diagnostic-only output (rules_skipped with 'unreachable' reason) rather than findings[]. Until then, keep them as findings.

TLS-001 on the [legacy] domain (F1) is NOT a path-sensitivity issue — TLS domain configs are global and apply whenever the domain is referenced. The v1.0 engine doesn't track which domains are bound to listeners, so it flags all weak-domain configs.
